selected_evidence.requirement: sudo commands are logged to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user and timestamp
selected_evidence.summary: After installing the sudoers snippet, subsequent sudo commands (run as root and as test user 'sudologtest') were recorded in /var/log/sudo-commands.log with timestamp, invoking user, PWD, and COMMAND fields.

selected_evidence.requirement: these entries are kept out of the general system log
selected_evidence.summary: Baseline showed sudo COMMAND= lines in /var/log/secure and journalctl before the change; after adding 'Defaults !syslog', tail/grep of /var/log/secure, /var/log/messages, and journalctl -t sudo show no COMMAND= entries for any subsequent sudo invocation (root or sudologtest).

selected_evidence.requirement: sudoers config is syntactically valid and correctly installed
selected_evidence.summary: visudo -cf validated the snippet before install; final file placed at /etc/sudoers.d/command-logging with 0440 root:root permissions.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline captured before restart
selected_evidence.summary: Captured baseline boot_id (cce73776-a7f7-4f32-b822-95d105c52a64) along with sudoers config and current log file contents prior to reboot.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart executed safely with acknowledgement returned before disconnect
selected_evidence.summary: Issued 'systemctl reboot' backgrounded so the trigger command returned before the connection dropped; stream closure confirms the reboot proceeded.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 restart proven via changed boot identity
selected_evidence.summary: Node was unreachable immediately after reboot (connection reset), then came back with boot_id 316d203c-8b2b-4777-97e6-b48341fd9a35, differing from the pre-restart boot_id, proving an actual restart occurred.

selected_evidence.requirement: node1 post-restart recovery: sudo command logging still functions correctly and stays out of general log
selected_evidence.summary: After reboot, sudoers config and log file content were intact; a fresh sudo command was correctly appended to /var/log/sudo-commands.log with user/timestamp, and no COMMAND= lines appeared in /var/log/secure, confirming full recovery of the required configuration and behavior.
